chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Safwan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is disliked for the man, when he returns from travel, to visit his family at night until morning.

key_terms.أَهْلَهُ: His family/wife - the person being visited.
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: Travel/Journey - the context triggering this specific etiquette.
key_terms.حَتَّى يُصْبِحَ: Until morning - the recommended waiting period before visiting.
key_terms.لَيْلًا: At night - the specific time period mentioned.
key_terms.يَطْرُقَ: To visit/surprise - specifically implies visiting without prior notice or at an unexpected time.
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: Disliked (makruh) - a juristic ruling indicating preference for avoidance but not prohibition.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette for a husband returning home from travel regarding intimacy with his wife?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines a specific marital etiquette (adab) where it is disliked (makruh) for a husband to surprise his wife at night immediately upon returning from travel, ensuring she is rested and composed. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling balances the husband's desire for intimacy with the wife's right to privacy and comfort, reflecting the broader Islamic principle of gentleness in conjugal relations. It highlights the Prophet’s family’s emphasis on psychological and physical consideration within the domestic sphere.
